root_idea.summary: The root centers on fleeing or moving away, especially escaping from danger or pursuit.
root_idea.development: From the basic idea of fleeing, Classical Arabic develops causative and reciprocal flight, refuge and places of refuge, and several specialized extensions. These broader developments are kept distinct from the Quranic noun.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested nominal form, normalized from the accusative occurrence هَرَبًا to the citation form هَرَبٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: A nominal/verbal-noun use denoting the act or means of fleeing; in the Quranic occurrence, flight is presented as a possible means of escape.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flee to a refuge or seek refuge by fleeing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A directional refuge construction, exemplified by fleeing to God for refuge from punishment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To disappear into or be swallowed by the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage describing part of an object disappearing into the ground; the cited example concerns half of a peg or stake.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become extremely old, weak, or decrepit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal form equated with هَرِمَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make, cause, force, or compel someone to flee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Causative transitive usage of the derived forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wind: to raise and carry away dust, causing dust or dry herbage to accumulate on the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive usage with the wind as subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exert oneself intensely in going away or in an undertaking; to immerse oneself in an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for strenuous departure or flight and, in an affair, for taking extraordinary pains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go or travel far into or through the land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A locative usage referring to extensive travel through the country.
Reciprocal usage in which the parties flee mutually or from one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The thin layer or caul of fat covering the stomach and intestines.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal anatomical term, equated with ثَرْبُ البَطْنِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مَا لَهُ هَارِبٌ وَلَا قَارِبٌ, one returning from water; the idiom may consequently mean having nothing or no people, or having no one who flees from or approaches him, hence being insignificant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed idiom contrasting هَارِبٌ, one returning from water, with قَارِبٌ, one going to it; alternative idiomatic interpretations are attested.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place to which one flees; a place of refuge; figuratively, a person who serves as a refuge.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The personal-refuge usage is explicitly figurative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who strives or exerts himself in an affair; in another reported usage, one who comes fleeing in fright.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression جاء مُهْرِبًا, with an alternative interpretation referring to fleeing fearfully.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wooden implement drawn back and forth over the soil after sowing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An agricultural implement, described as a piece of wood or a trunk section dragged over the ground.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Basic meaning of fleeing is the lexical basis of the Quranic noun.
Water-related lexical meaning and fixed idiom.
Active-participial usage in the cited expression.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is the nominal accusative هَرَبًا; the public headword is normalized to the citation form هَرَبٌ. The dialectal هَرِبَ meaning “to become decrepit” is kept separate from this Quranic noun.
